mainEntity.name: Is Local Storage Always Faster Than Shared Storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the device level, yes. In practice the gap depends on your fabric. A well-built NVMe over TCP or SPDK iSCSI target retains around 80% of local IOPS. A 1G iSCSI link to a spinning array will be several times slower than local disk.

mainEntity.name: Can I Use Local Storage and Still Offer High Availability?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not through the platform's HA feature. SolusVM requires Shared LVM over iSCSI or NFS for a failover domain. You can offer application-level redundancy across two local-storage instances on separate hosts, but that's a customer-side design.

mainEntity.name: Does NFS Work for Production VPS Storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: It works and SolusVM supports it, but NFS is a remote storage type and some operations take longer as a result. It's the lower-effort path into shared storage. Shared LVM over iSCSI is the faster one.

mainEntity.name: What About Snapshots on Shared Storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Shared LVM implementation in SolusVM doesn't support snapshots or Thin LVM, so if snapshot-based backups are part of your product, that constraint picks your storage type for you.

mainEntity.name: Which Model Has the Lower Total Cost of Ownership?

acceptedAnswer.text: Local storage, at small scale, by a wide margin. Shared storage catches up once stranded capacity across many nodes exceeds the replication overhead, and once manual recovery starts showing up in your ticket volume.

@graph.name: How to Choose Between Shared Storage and Local Storage for VPS Infrastructure
@graph.description: A five-step decision for hosting providers picking a storage model for their SolusVM compute resources.

step.name: Decide whether you are selling automatic failover
step.text: High Availability in SolusVM requires every compute resource in the failover domain to run KVM and use Shared LVM over iSCSI or NFS. If failover is on your feature list, local storage is not eligible.

step.name: Measure the latency your workloads actually tolerate
step.text: Local NVMe answers random 4K reads in roughly 20 to 70 microseconds. A network round trip adds 250 to 450 microseconds over NVMe/TCP, more over conventional iSCSI. Web workloads absorb that. Small synchronous database writes do not.

step.name: Cost the storage fabric honestly
step.text: Three-way replication returns roughly a third of raw capacity as usable space. Add 25G networking, a dedicated storage VLAN, and the CPU the storage path consumes on every node.

step.name: Check what you give up on shared storage
step.text: The SolusVM Shared LVM implementation does not support Thin LVM or snapshots, which removes thin provisioning and incremental ThinLVM backups from that tier.

step.name: Tier the estate and price each tier separately
step.text: Put high-IOPS plans on local ThinLVM nodes and managed or business-tier plans on a shared LVM or NFS failover domain. Charge for the second tier, because the hardware costs more.
